arxiv-1809-08826.title: Information-Weighted Neural Cache Language Models for ASR
arxiv-1809-08826.creator: Lyan Verwimp, Joris Pelemans, Hugo Van hamme, Patrick Wambacq
arxiv-1809-08826.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Lyan Verwimp, Joris Pelemans, Hugo Van hamme, Patrick Wambacq. Neural cache language models (LMs) extend the idea of regular cache language models by making the cache probability dependent on the similarity between the current context and the context of the words in the cache. We make an extensive comparison of ‘regular’ cache models with neural cache models, both in terms of perplexity and WER after rescoring first-pass ASR results.

arxiv-2306-06670.title: Shear, writhe and filaments: turbulence in the high latitude molecular cloud MBM 40
arxiv-2306-06670.creator: Marco Monaci, Loris Magnani, Steven N.Shore, Henrik Olofsson, Mackenzie R. Joy
arxiv-2306-06670.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marco Monaci, Loris Magnani, Steven N.Shore, Henrik Olofsson, Mackenzie R. Joy. It is almost banal to say that the interstellar medium (ISM) is structurally and thermodynamically complex. But the variety of the governing processes, including stellar feedback, renders the investigation challenging. High latitude molecular clouds (HLMCs) with no evidence of internal star formation, such as MBM 40, are excellent sites for studying the chemistry and dynamic evolution of the cold neutral ISM.

arxiv-2406-07638.title: QuReed
arxiv-2406-07638.creator: Simon Sekavčnik, Kareem H. El-Safty, Janis Nötzel
arxiv-2406-07638.description: Abstract We present QuReed , an open-source quantum simulation framework designed to bridge gaps between quantum theory, experimental community and engineering. With Quantum Mechanics maturing and holding significant potential beyond quantum computing, the need for physically accurate simulations becomes critical. QuReed offers peer-reviewed simulation models, providing researchers and engineers with reliable tools for exploring quantum communication protocols and applications.

arxiv-2407-14352.title: Vision-Based Power Line Cables and Pylons Detection for Low Flying Aircraft
arxiv-2407-14352.creator: Jakub Gwizdała, Doruk Oner, Soumava Kumar Roy, Mian Akbar Shah, Ad Eberhard, Ivan Egorov, Philipp Krüsi, Grigory Yakushev, Pascal Fua

Power lines are dangerous for low-flying aircrafts, especially in low-visibility conditions. Thus, a vision-based system able to analyze the aircraft’s surroundings and to provide the pilots with a “second pair of eyes” can contribute to enhancing their safety.

arxiv-2501-09973.description: Abstract We report the determination of the Landé g J g_{J} factor and Zeeman coefficients for the ground-state of 171 Yb + , relevant to microwave quantum frequency standards (QFSs). pmc-10808655.creator: Minsu Kim, Myeongsu Kim, Yong-Gu Yeo, Young-Tae Lee, Jae-Ik Han

The objective of this study was to investigate the prevalence and characteristics of antimicrobial resistance pattern in Escherichia coli and Enterococcus faecalis isolated from the feces of captive wild animals in a zoo.

pmc-11452402.title: Artificial intelligence in commercial fracture detection products: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy
pmc-11452402.creator: Julius Husarek, Silvan Hess, Sam Razaeian, Thomas D. Ruder, Stephan Sehmisch, Martin Müller, Emmanouil Liodakis
pmc-11452402.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Conventional radiography (CR) is primarily utilized for fracture diagnosis. Artificial intelligence (AI) for CR is a rapidly growing field aimed at enhancing efficiency and increasing diagnostic accuracy. However, the diagnostic performance of commercially available AI fracture detection solutions (CAAI-FDS) for CR in various anatomical regions, their synergy with human assessment, as well as the influence of industry funding on reported accuracy are unknown. Peer-reviewed diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) studies were identified through a systematic review on Pubmed and Embase.

pmc-13031678.creator: Bartosz Mierzejewski, Zuzanna Michalska, Dominika Kulma, Aleksandra Bos, Wladyslawa Streminska, Zbigniew Bartoszewicz, Edyta Brzoska
pmc-13031678.description: CD146 + interstitial cells are myogenic progenitors which contribute to skeletal muscle regeneration. However, their role in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains unclear. We compared CD146 + cells from wild-type and mdx mice, revealing distinct molecular and functional differences. Mdx CD146 + differentiated less efficiently into myoblasts and multinucleated myotubes but more efficiently into fibroblasts and adipocytes in vitro.

Despite its urgency, the lack of diagnostic and predictive biomarkers continues to hinder the development of effective prevention and treatment strategies.

pmc-13040825.title: Faecal microbiome profiling uncovers putative biomarkers for piglets resilient to post-weaning diarrhoea
pmc-13040825.creator: Mattia Pirolo, Moiz Khan Sherwani, Carmen Espinosa-Gongora, Esben Østergaard Eriksen, Clara Tassinato, Antton Alberdi, Luca Guardabassi
pmc-13040825.description: BackgroundPost-weaning diarrhoea (PWD) is a major health and economic concern in intensive pig production. In this study, we hypothesized that the faecal microbiome, sampled before disease onset, could provide early prognostic markers of PWD risk and applied a machine-learning framework to identify biomarkers predictive of piglet susceptibility or resilience to PWD.

pmc-13074703.title: Degradation Mechanism of Mechanical Properties of Concrete in a High Hydraulic Pressure Environment

pmc-13189357.title: Modeling cell migratory persistence through temporal correlations and angular noise
pmc-13189357.creator: Ignacio Montenegro-Rojas, Martín Andaur-Lobos, Karol Soler-Orozco, Diego Castelli-Lacunza, Cristina Bertocchi, Anastasios Matzavinos, Andrea Ravasio, Haroldo V. Ribeiro, Haroldo V. Ribeiro, Haroldo V. Ribeiro
pmc-13189357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The persistence of cell migration is a fundamental property of motile behavior, enabling cells to maintain directionality while adapting to fluctuations and external cues. This feature underlies essential processes such as development, immune responses, and cancer invasion. Classical mathematical models have offered key insights into directed migration, yet they often neglect temporal correlations arising from cellular mechanisms that stabilize polarity and protrusion dynamics.

pmc-13317147.title: Atypical Presentation of Rapidly Progressive Guillain–Barré Syndrome With Dysautonomia in an Adolescent With Persistent Mycoplasma pneumoniae Infection: A Case Report
pmc-13317147.creator: Madhu Parna Chakrabarti, Richard Sultan, Daniel Ruderfer, Katherine Hickey
pmc-13317147.description: BackgroundGuillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune‐mediated polyradiculoneuropathy and the leading cause of acute flaccid paralysis in children. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a frequent antecedent infection in pediatric GBS and has been associated with a severe, rapidly progressive course with heterogeneous neurologic manifestations, creating diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.
